card.name: Punctuation in technical or patent descriptions
card.fires_on: Commas, periods and small linking words that end or continue a clause in technical explanations, mostly patent text ("according to a preferred embodiment,") and definitions of tests or methods.

modes.label: Patent clause punctuation
modes.description: Comma or period closing a stock phrase in patent-style text about methods or data processing systems.
modes.example: According to a preferred embodiment<<,>> an automator is attached to a Java

modes.label: Definition sentence end
modes.description: Period after a short explanatory definition of a procedure or process.
modes.example: such as cancer cells, in the bone<<.>> A very small amount of radioactive material is

modes.label: Linking words in technical phrasing
modes.description: Small words such as to, that or implemented inside patent figure descriptions or quiz questions.
modes.example: How many hundredths are needed<< to>> make one? (100)

card.plain: It fires on commas and periods in technical, patent-style descriptions, right before the next clause begins.
